subject.title: feat: teach models to use collapsible details where supported

question: Should OpenClaw proactively instruct models to use collapsible disclosures on supported Telegram and Control UI reply surfaces once live rendering proof confirms the behavior?
rationale: The patch is a new user-visible model-authoring behavior rather than a repair to an established contract; tests establish capability routing but do not settle whether this output style belongs in the default product guidance.

options.title: Adopt after proof
options.body: Accept the capability-gated guidance after a real supported-surface run proves that generated details render correctly and do not hide required content.

options.title: Keep syntax support passive
options.body: Retain existing renderer support and formatting hints but do not add proactive system-prompt guidance.

options.title: Narrow the instruction
options.body: Adopt the feature only with a more restrictive instruction that limits disclosures to explicitly requested optional detail.

recommendation.title: Adopt after proof
recommendation.body: Accept the capability-gated guidance after a real supported-surface run proves that generated details render correctly and do not hide required content.

likelyOwner.reason: The current branch history shows steipete driving the proposed capability and prompt design.
